roles.title: Parties reviewer
roles.mirrors: defense counsel mapping parties and contractor tiers from the records
roles.brief: You are the parties reviewer on a construction claim. You work out, from the records only, who the parties are, what role each had on the project, and how they are related: who contracted with whom, who represented whom, who reviewed whose submittals, who supplied what, who inspected.
roles.default_focus: every organisation and person named, their roles, the relationships between them, and names written differently for the same party
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

roles.title: Technical reviewer
roles.brief: You are the technical reviewer on a construction claim. You record, from the records only, the design requirements, submittals and how they were dispositioned, tests and their results, deviations from requirements, and when each happened. You state facts, never causes.
roles.default_focus: dated events: design requirements and values, submittals and approvals, tests and results, problems reported, repairs, and what the documents do not contain
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

verifier_rules: Every quote must be found on the page it cites, after collapsing whitespace and folding curly quotes and dashes. Case, spelling and word order must match.
A quote on a production label (a cover sheet or divider added when the claim file was assembled) is refused.
A quote on a page outside the readable claim file is refused.
An event dated as the document's own date must match the date read from the document, with its source span.
An event dated from the text must have a quote that shows that date.
A party's name must appear in its quotes; a relationship's two parties must both appear in its quotes.
An alias is accepted only when one quote shows both names.
A claim with no citation is shown as interpretation, never as fact.
One failed citation refuses the whole claim. Refused claims are kept with their reasons, not softened.
harness.negative_rule: Each role proposes what the claim file does not contain at the end of the run, with search terms that would find a counter-example. A negative is accepted only if every in-scope page was read in the run and a phrase search for each term finds nothing in scope.

memory_collections.pages / documents / metadata: the ingested claim file, written only by ingestion
memory_collections.coverage: every read and search, with the pages it covered
memory_collections.refusals: refused claims with the verifier's reasons
memory_collections.workers: every reader started: role, documents, focus, tokens
memory_collections.trace: one event per step of the run
memory_collections.checkpoints: LangGraph run state, so a run can stop and resume
memory_collections.outputs: chronology, party map, exhibits and coverage report
memory_collections.cache: Reducto and Gemini responses, so nothing is paid for twice

answer_key.summary: About 11 p.m., the M1 row of anchors in eastbound ceiling module EB081 pulls out. The suspended concrete ceiling swings down onto a passing car, and the passenger is killed.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: As the car approached the end of the I-90 connector tunnel, a section of the tunnel’s suspended concrete ceiling detached from the tunnel roof and fell onto the vehicle.

answer_key.summary: During on-scene work, investigators measure every anchor left in the portal roof. Many have displaced downward, and the displaced share is greatest in the most heavily loaded rows.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: After the accident, 161 of the 634 remaining adhesive anchors supporting the D Street portal ceiling were found to have measurable displacement,

answer_key.summary: The NTSB Materials Laboratory examines the 20 failed M1-row anchors and others from the tunnel. Yellowed epoxy appears only on anchors that had displaced (0.5 inch or more), and on one failed anchor it reaches about 4 inches up the embedment.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: 13 of the 20 anchors in that row showed a yellow discoloration found only on displaced anchors.

answer_key.summary: MIT's FTIR analysis for the NTSB matches all epoxy samples from the tunnel to Powers Fast Set, not Standard Set. An FHWA report states that construction invoices also show a fast-set formula was used.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy at MIT showed that all of the samples from the tunnels, including the samples from the accident site, matched to the Fast Set reference samples.

answer_key.summary: The FHWA runs sustained-load (creep) tests on anchors still installed in the westbound portal roof. In 3 of the 9 rigorous tests the displacement never stabilizes; two anchors pull out completely.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: During the sustained load tests, two anchors pulled completely free of the tunnel roof.

answer_key.summary: In 82-day FHWA laboratory creep tests, anchors set with Power-Fast Fast Set creep at every load, and those loaded to 4,000 lb fail. Standard Set anchors barely move under the same conditions.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The testing showed that anchors installed with the Powers Fast Set epoxy, using best practices, exhibited significant and continued displacement (creep) when subjected to loads as low as 1,000 pounds.

Owner MassHighway (par-799eb35d02ed, eve-f672617e5e19) and the Massachusetts Turnpike Authority (par-540841c5c44b, rel-92b4c7802043) retained management consultant Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) (par-d2937ce7d22a, rel-f8d64c7bfe48, rel-ad4cd7edab4e) to oversee construction and review contractor submittals (rel-f8ccff2f756b, rel-6b3bd7d26740, rel-ca1089bdfbee). MassHighway contracted with general contractor Walsh Construction of Illinois for C05B1 (rel-c9b11dd4709d, eve-ed7ee034aead), which subcontracted core drilling to Engineered Products Company (rel-6fdfe394c623, eve-6338ebe22c19). For C09B2, Modern Continental Construction (MCC) acted as general contractor (par-92d0926ec09f, par-b01284cf6d72), with Powers Fasteners supplying adhesive anchors (par-534e79c4e61d, rel-21b133bb4b61), Conam Inspection providing testing services (rel-71f634367c44, par-730b650dbd7e), and Environmental Interiors subcontracted for ceiling systems (par-027707240799, eve-62d19936895d). Design and calculation review responsibilities involved section designers including Gannett Fleming (par-e411ff9caca2, rel-ee98a1fbd01b) and SIGMA Engineering (par-4e794c933599). Formal notices show B/PB issued Deficiency Report No. 001 to MCC in December 1999 regarding anchor pull-out at module HOV 079 (eve-8a78cbce28ea, eve-18ba4fcd153d), which B/PB closed in January 2001 upon verification of corrective retesting and replacements (eve-54393090dddb, eve-f1010b357a9e). Testing cost disputes initiated by MCC under CP-022 (eve-753679cd757c, eve-7a335ab9cd5a) culminated in the execution of Field Work Order Modification No. 158FW by MTA in March 2001 (eve-823cb8bdb743, eve-5a58bcd9c9c2).

The record explicitly confirms that "Coring for the installation of anchors for Phase 1 of testing began on October 11, 2006." While the record notes that "61 additional holes were cored on October 17th", the start of coring for Phase 1 anchor testing is established as October 11, 2006, directly supporting eve-c5361458d2ef.

The record directly corroborates eve-5347b574069f with substantive narrative evidence from the report, noting: "There was one laborer setting anchor bolts in HOV. He was working from a Terex TE44 boom lift. The bolts were installed without screens to hold the epoxy, and without blowing the holes out w/ compressed air." By contrast, eve-23e4a6fb8b9c provides only a header quote ("28-JUL-1999 07:00-15:00 3 996910 JAMES BARRETT") without any textual documentation supporting bolt counts, mock-up location, or screen installation details.

The record fully supports counsel's claim with the direct quote: "MCC had one laborer setting anchor bolts in the EB bore. By end of day, 46 bolts were installed. There was no testing of anchor bolts today." In contrast, the engineer's quote ("04-AUG-1999 07:00-15:00 3 996910 JAMES BARRETT") fails to provide any textual support for the testing results, failures, or Conam Inspection details alleged in eve-7c248c63c4d5.

Claim eve-c491d1e9fe35 is directly and accurately supported by the documented evidence stating that "On November 28, 2006 the sustained load testing was completed. All anchors still holding load were unloaded and monitored overnight to quantify recovery, if any, of the epoxy." In contrast, the quote for eve-a982bf7f6236 only references a singular anchor ("The load was then reapplied to the anchor on November 7, 2006"), failing to substantiate that loads were reapplied across tests 1, 2, and 6.

The record directly supports claim eve-8b435163fe92 regarding the October 31, 2006 installation date as documented by the quote 'Anchors 1-77 installed by Tim Tuggle and Justin Ocel on 31 October 2006', properly aligning with the engineer's technical scope and precisely matching the stated installation personnel and anchor set, whereas claim eve-bc81caae5994 references a separate later installation quoting 'Anchors 78-98 installed by Tim Tuggle and Justin Ocel on 2 November 2006'.

Claim eve-144301180291 is better supported by the record as it accurately aligns with the document quote "Anchors 78-98 installed by Tim Tuggle and Justin Ocel on 2 November 2006", properly attributing the installation to Tim Tuggle and Justin Ocel on 2006-11-02. In contrast, claim eve-c762ff914143 cites "Anchors 1-77 installed by Tim Tuggle and Justin Ocel on 31 October 2006" but introduces the unsupported descriptor "test" and omits the actors identified in the source text.

The claim file documents the administrative, contractual, and technical records for tunnel ceiling construction and subsequent investigative evaluations. Project owner MassHighway (par-799eb35d02ed) and the Massachusetts Turnpike Authority (par-540841c5c44b), which represented MassHighway (rel-92b4c7802043), retained Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) (par-d2937ce7d22a) as management consultant representing the owner (rel-ad4cd7edab4e, rel-f8d64c7bfe48). Gannett Fleming acted as section design consultant designing for B/PB (rel-ee98a1fbd01b, par-929edec2c240). General contractor Modern Continental Construction (par-a55d7cea209d, par-92d0926ec09f) was overseen by B/PB (rel-65c7b5db73fc), which reviewed contractor submittals (rel-6b3bd7d26740, rel-ec0bb60c7eb3). MassHighway also contracted with Walsh Construction of Illinois (rel-c9b11dd4709d, par-659157f7c0a7), overseen by B/PB (rel-2677e4f29ba7, rel-ca1089bdfbee), which subcontracted drilling to Engineered Products Company (rel-6fdfe394c623, rel-071ebbedfaf8). Fasteners and epoxy adhesives were supplied and manufactured by Powers Fasteners, Inc. (par-458eca7365fb, par-78d2dde8ade5, rel-21b133bb4b61) and Sika Corporation (par-0b036ce4c523, par-7685332a6909). During construction, Conam Inspection performed pull-out testing under subcontract to Modern Continental (rel-71f634367c44, rel-2b4775a5d0d4, par-303c9335b051), and CEL Consulting inspected for Powers Fasteners (rel-623b98b5abf2). Following the ceiling collapse, testing and investigative procedures were led by the National Transportation Safety Board (par-32e53f799e1c, par-947fc522d291) and Federal Highway Administration (par-73990e76d679, rel-dae0ec910d2d), supported by testing and analysis from Bodycote Polymer – Broutman Laboratory (rel-9241d1052b3b, par-8941a60d78cc), Standard Testing and Engineering Company (rel-eb2a7d768555), Trace Laboratories-East (rel-1765beb1e54f), Laser Techniques Company (rel-fd7dd7bbcfd7), and evidence custody by the Massachusetts State Police (par-4329b520d7fc, par-c4bbbfbe3795).

decision.summary: Between 1996 and 1997, preliminary designs and sketches established ceiling support configurations, fireproofing details, and anchor criteria (eve-206664b7420a, eve-d2dc81106a60, eve-ac510b8bc45b, eve-0e493da9d74f). In late 1999, following observed adhesive anchor displacement, Powers Fasteners provided repair recommendations to Modern Continental Construction (eve-1e3678e9d0d7). Reviewers rejected proposed fix DR-001 and mandated repair and proof-testing protocols, issued under Letter C09B2-0498 (eve-d97538a8cbdb, eve-c2db75fda81d). Modern Continental submitted repair procedures under Submittal 723.480-016 A and B, which incorporated hole cleaning requirements from field engineering review and received status 2N conditional approval in February 2000 (eve-1ef5d0e010c3, eve-c93ddd6131db, eve-51e8cb2cf830, eve-7298f5b12f08). Concurrently, anchor submittals referencing evaluation reports ER-4514 and subsequent ESR-1531 were processed and conditionally approved (eve-fc59578bf290, eve-6ba8d2f5695c, eve-7c53376d069f, eve-25c03695f356, eve-885b8b055049, eve-19113756abbc). Conam Inspection conducted nondestructive testing on anchor resin in July 2000 (eve-e557f6611aa6, rel-2b4775a5d0d4), and record drawings were established in January 2004 (eve-07a22ea4b6e5). On July 10, 2006, ceiling panels detached in the eastbound I-90 Seaport Access Tunnel (eve-f7af997d6bca, eve-aeefe27848ad), prompting post-incident downward displacement measurements on remaining anchors and subsequent testing by the NTSB and FHWA (eve-1d10da247b93, eve-a296ac0ff898, eve-45e82670f27a, rel-dae0ec910d2d).

decision.summary: Project records document the contractual tiers and oversight structure for Contracts C05B1 and C09B2. Owner MassHighway (par-799eb35d02ed, eve-f672617e5e19) and the Massachusetts Turnpike Authority (par-540841c5c44b, rel-92b4c7802043) retained management consultant Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) (par-d2937ce7d22a, rel-f8d64c7bfe48, rel-ad4cd7edab4e) to oversee construction and review contractor submittals (rel-f8ccff2f756b, rel-6b3bd7d26740, rel-ca1089bdfbee). MassHighway contracted with general contractor Walsh Construction of Illinois for C05B1 (rel-c9b11dd4709d, eve-ed7ee034aead), which subcontracted core drilling to Engineered Products Company (rel-6fdfe394c623, eve-6338ebe22c19). For C09B2, Modern Continental Construction (MCC) acted as general contractor (par-92d0926ec09f, par-b01284cf6d72), with Powers Fasteners supplying adhesive anchors (par-534e79c4e61d, rel-21b133bb4b61), Conam Inspection providing testing services (rel-71f634367c44, par-730b650dbd7e), and Environmental Interiors subcontracted for ceiling systems (par-027707240799, eve-62d19936895d). Design and calculation review responsibilities involved section designers including Gannett Fleming (par-e411ff9caca2, rel-ee98a1fbd01b) and SIGMA Engineering (par-4e794c933599). Formal notices show B/PB issued Deficiency Report No. 001 to MCC in December 1999 regarding anchor pull-out at module HOV 079 (eve-8a78cbce28ea, eve-18ba4fcd153d), which B/PB closed in January 2001 upon verification of corrective retesting and replacements (eve-54393090dddb, eve-f1010b357a9e). Testing cost disputes initiated by MCC under CP-022 (eve-753679cd757c, eve-7a335ab9cd5a) culminated in the execution of Field Work Order Modification No. 158FW by MTA in March 2001 (eve-823cb8bdb743, eve-5a58bcd9c9c2).

members.job: You are the claim professional who owns this construction-defect liability claim file. You assign work to defense counsel and, once you approve its retention, the forensic engineer. Your job is to get every document read by the right role, follow up open questions, rule disputes on the evidence, and close the claim file. It cannot exclude documents: every document is read by some role.
members.sees: the document index (type, date, author, recipient, pages, who read it), counts of verified and refused claims, open tasks and disputes, reports received. Never page text.
can: assign counsel and work, with a focus
retain the forensic engineer, on request or on its own initiative
close the claim file (only when the code's close check passes)
write the case brief from verified claims
members.never: reads pages, makes claims about their content, states fault or coverage

members.title: Defense counsel
members.job: You are defense counsel on a construction-defect claim, working for the claim professional. From the records only, you establish the parties and contractor tiers, how they are related (who contracted with whom, who represented whom, who reviewed whose submittals, who supplied what, who inspected), and who approved or was responsible for what, as the documents show it. You state documented facts, never fault or liability.
members.sees: the document index, its own verified claims and open questions; page text only through its readers
can: plan what to read and start readers
review its readers' claims and read more (up to 2 follow-up rounds)
ask the lead to retain an engineer
raise and answer requests, open disputes
members.never: retains the engineer without approval; states fault

members.title: Forensic engineer
members.mirrors: the forensic expert retained with the carrier's approval
members.job: You are the forensic engineer retained by defense counsel, with the claim professional's approval. From the records only, you set out the technical record: design requirements and values, submittals and how they were dispositioned, tests with their methods and results, deviations from requirements, repairs, and when each happened. You state documented facts, never an opinion on cause.
members.sees: as counsel, for its own documents and claims
can: as counsel, except asking for an expert
members.waits_for: expert.approved: it cannot start before the lead approves it

members.title: Readers
members.job: Read whole documents (long ones in page windows) for one role and focus; return dated events, parties, relationships, aliases and open questions, each with an exact quote.
members.sees: only their batch (about 40k characters), plus up to 2 short documents it cites by reference number
can: one automatic repair of refused claims

members.title: Dispatcher, verifier, assembly
members.mirrors: the claims system and file rules
members.job: Turns events into tasks and runs them in parallel; checks every claim against the page; tests absences; decides whether the file may close; assembles the chronology, party map and exhibits.
can: hold a task until what it waits for exists
expire stuck tasks and tell the lead
stop the run on a guard

verifier_rules: Every quote must be found on the page it cites. Whitespace, curly quotes and dashes are folded, and a word may be joined across a hyphen at a line break; case, spelling and word order must match.
A quote on a production label (a cover sheet or divider added when the claim file was assembled), or on a page outside the readable claim file, is refused.
An event dated as the document's own date must match the date read from the document; an event dated from the text must have a quote that shows that date.

A party's name must appear in its quotes, ignoring case, punctuation and corporate suffixes; a relationship's two parties must both appear. At assembly, a name also appears through a verified alias quoted in the claim.
An alias is accepted only when one quote shows both names.
A refused claim is sent back to its reader once with the page and the reason; if it still fails it is kept with its reasons, never softened.
team_spec.negative_rule: At the end, each role proposes what the claim file does not contain, with search terms that would find a counter-example. An absence is accepted only if every in-scope page was read in the run and a phrase search for each term finds nothing in scope.

memory.events: the append-only event log: every message between roles, with its cause; change streams wake consumers
memory.tasks: one task per event a role must handle: waits-for, deadline, state, outcome
memory.reservations: which task holds which document, per role (unique index), so no document is read twice by a role
memory.coverage: every page handed to a reader, with the role and focus, logged before the model runs
memory.findings / refusals: verified claims, and refused ones with the verifier's reasons
memory.disputes: conflicting claims on the same page and the lead's ruling
memory.model_calls: every model call: who, for which task, tokens, cost, the decision and its reasoning summary
memory.workers: every reader: documents, pages, focus, claims kept and refused
memory.checkpoints: LangGraph state of each role's task (plan, read, review, close), so a task can resume
memory.pages / documents / metadata / sources: the ingested claim file (GridFS for the PDFs, Atlas Search on page text)
memory.cache: model and parser answers, so a finished run replays for free

comparisons.label: 8 Claude agents · no harness
